name: Multiband, 3 bands at 425 Hz and 5.5 kHz
notes: Fancy MultiComp against KolinMB (Analog Obsession, free) on KolinMB's three bands: crossovers at 425 Hz and 5.5 kHz, attack 10 ms, release 400 ms. KolinMB has no threshold or ratio: each band's Input drives it, and a level below threshold passes unchanged. Its drives (Low 14, Mid 30, High 12 dB) match Fancy's 4:1 at -20 dB at 1 kHz only (-3.6 against -4.9 dB at -10 dBFS, -11.6 against -11.7 at 0 dBFS, the same on two runs); its low and high bands then compress 10 to 20 dB harder. Keep the band Output entries: KolinMB's band Outputs only go from 0 dB up, so FancyBench lands them on 0 dB, but without them KolinMB doesn't compress at these drives (seen, not explained). So CPU, latency, aliasing and clicks compare like for like; response and THD show character, not the same settings. The like-for-like test is multiband.json, against Convergence Free.
